title: Right derived functors and coherent nonnegative total complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with ordinary derived categories and K-injective right derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $\Delta$ be the small category of finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and order-preserving maps, and let $K:\Delta\to\operatorname{Ch}^{\ge0}(\mathcal A)$ be a strict cosimplicial diagram of nonnegative cochain complexes. Write $K^{n,q}=K([n])^q$ and $\delta=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i d^i$ for the alternating coface differential. Define $T(K)^r=\bigoplus_{n+q=r}K^{n,q}$ with differential $\delta+(-1)^n d_K$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], and write $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms.
There are compatible nonnegative injective replacements of the complexes $K([n])$, retaining all cosimplicial operators, for which the resulting resolved total computes $RF(QT(K))$. In particular there is a canonical isomorphism in $D(\mathcal B)$
$$\chi_{F,K}:RF(QT(K))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{n\ge0}RF(QK([n])).$$
The right hand side means the total of this coherently resolved diagram, rather than a total assigned to a diagram only in the ordinary derived category. If a nonnegative resolution degree $s$ is added, only triples $n,q,s\ge0$ with $n+q+s=r$ contribute to total degree $r$. The comparison is induced by the right-derived comparison maps on these resolutions and the canonical finite-biproduct identifications.
It is independent of compatible resolution choices and natural in strict cosimplicial chain maps. For a strict augmentation $\operatorname{const}(A)\to K$ with $A$ a nonnegative complex, let $a:A\to T(K)$ have component $a^0$ in cosimplicial degree zero and zero in higher cosimplicial degrees. Then $\chi_{F,K}\circ RF(Qa)$ is the totalized derived augmentation $RF(QA)\to\operatorname{Tot}_{n\ge0}RF(QK([n]))$. These assertions include compatible maps of augmented diagrams. No preservation of injectives by an unrelated exact functor is assumed.
